2. Otherwise, write separate lists of even and odd numbers (2, 4, 6, 8 ... and 1, 3, 5, 7, ...).
   - If the remainder is 2, swap 1 and 3 in the odd list and move 5 to the end (i.e., ... 3, 1, 7, 5, 9, 11, ...).
   - If the remainder is 3, move 2 to the end of the even list and 1,3 to the end of the odd list.
3. Append the odd list to the even list and place queens in the rows corresponding to these numbers (i.e., a 1 in the first position indicates the queen is in the first row and first column, ... )."
